question: Can deliberate, gradient-free edits to Stockfish 19 NNUE improve play?
hypothesis: The final affine bias is an interpretable side-to-move intercept. Small, material-tapered changes could improve the treatment of initiative at shallow search. Test both signs because the correct direction is unknown. This is a hypothesis, not a diagnosed defect in Stockfish.
method: Manually specified direct NNUE parameter edits; no gradients, training, fitted optimizer, engine code changes, or strength limiting.

protocol.selection_rule: Choose the highest screening score, breaking ties by candidate order. Confirmation uses a disjoint precommitted set of opening positions. Confirmation is reported even if screening fails.
protocol.interpretation: Small exploratory experiment. Fixed-node, shallow-search results do not establish a general Elo gain. No improvement claim unless independent confirmation is statistically convincing, and a longer test at realistic time controls would still be required.
